## Check current Python version

Python interpreter that compiles and runs your code. For this course, we will be using `Python 3`, so to check, if `Python 3` is already installed on your computer and follow the instructions for your Operating System (@VSCodePythonTutorial):

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Windows

To determine if your Windows computer already has `Python 3`:

1.  Go to **Start** on the Windows Taskbar to open the **Command Prompt** app.
    
2.  Enter **cmd** in the Windows search box and select the **Command Prompt App** in the **Best match** results.
    
3.  At the command prompt, enter the following command and then press Enter:
    
    > python --version

## macOS

To determine if your macOS computer already has `Python 3` installed:

1.  Open the Terminal app by pressing `Command + Spacebar key` combination to search by using Spotlight.
    
2.  At the command prompt, enter the following command:
    
> python --version
        

## Linux

Python is pre-installed on most Linux distributions (like Ubuntu). To determine if your Linux computer already has `Python 3` installed:

1.  Open a Linux terminal session.
    
2.  At the command prompt, enter the following command and then press Enter:
    
> python --version
    
:::

:::{callout-note}
Running `python --version` may not return a value, or may return an error message stating _'python' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file._ This indicates Python is not installed on your system.

But, if you see the word `Python` with a set of numbers separated by `.` characters, some version of Python is installed. Here's an example of the output you might see:
    
> Python 3.11
:::

As long as the first number is `3`, you have Python 3 installed on your computer. If not, you'll need to install Python 3. 

## Installation of Python 3

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Windows
1. To install [Python from python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/), use the Download Python button that appears first on the page to download the latest version.

::: {.callout-important} 
Make sure that you have admin access for installing the latest version of the Python on Windows.
::: 


2. Execute the file that you have downloaded. This program must be run with your computer's administrator privileges, so be prepared to enter your appropriate password if asked. Click on the option:

> Add Python 3.11 to PATH (or its Mac/Linux equivalent)

**Pay close attention to where on your computer Python is installed and write it down.**

## macOS

The system install of Python on macOS is not supported. Instead, a package management system like `Homebrew` is recommended. To install Python using Homebrew on macOS use `brew install python3` at the Terminal prompt.

::: {.callout-note} 
On macOS, make sure the location of your VSCode installation is included in your PATH environment variable.
::: 

## Linux
The built-in Python 3 installation on Linux works well, but to install other Python packages you must install `pip` with `apt` or `dnf` package mangement depending on your Linux versions.
:::
